acceptance: In a fixture repository, a branch that merges origin/main after evolve pr refresh is pushed by evolve ship --push-only, and the test is red without the fix
An ahead commit that is not on origin/main and not in the ship journal is still refused
A merge commit with no parent on the origin branch is still refused
docs/operations/wave-operations.md names the verb that pushes the branch after the merge

consumed.resolution: lane triage recorded it as shipped (operator 2026-11-13: the item touches no protected file and its console route had no reason; a lane can build it)

fix: Design first, with an architecture review and a security review. One candidate: runPushOnly counts as ahead only the commits that origin/main does not hold, because a commit on origin/main already landed through the train. The provenance rule for each other commit stays.

intake_override.reason: the fix changes the provenance rule of the ship gate, which a lane cannot review for itself; the console holds the blocked branch

notes: Evidence 2026-11-11, worktree dev/cl-g4c, merge 324279b5d of origin/main 710b617a8 into PR 1397: ship --push-only --dry-run refused 63 ahead commits, all from main. A plain manual ship reports no staged changes. No sanctioned verb pushes the merge, so a PR that conflicts in a generated file cannot follow the documented refresh path.

summary: The operations guide says to merge origin/main, run evolve pr refresh and continue the merge. The ship gate then has no verb that pushes the result: push-only reads rev-list origin/<branch>..HEAD, which holds each main commit, and the ship journal of the worktree has none of them.
title: ship --push-only refuses a branch that merged origin/main, so a refreshed PR cannot be pushed
